excerpt: Lesson Plan Breeds of Livestock: Cattle   Lesson Overview Objectives: 1.     To identify breeds of cattle. 2.     To understand the origins and characteristics of cattle breeds. 3.     To analyze the importance of specific cattle breeds in livestock production.   Class 1 Essential Questions: 1.     What general terminology is associated with cattle? 2.     What are the origins, physical characteristics, traits and usages of dairy breeds?   Step 1: View the image of a Holstein cow, Brahman cow and Angus cow. Consider the question “what differences do you see physically in these three breeds of cattle, and how may this impact their use in livestock production”. Be prepared for a class discussion of your responses. Step 2: Access the Action Plan , Vocabulary Handout and Key Concepts . ·        The Action Plan lays out a list of tasks for you to complete during the lesson. ·        The Vocabulary Handout is a list of terms used throughout the lesson. ·        The Key Concepts is an outline which identifies the main ideas presented in the lesson which you can fill in to aid in note taking during the lesson. Step 3: View the Dairy Breeds PowerPoint ® segment. ·        This segment is 24 slides long. ·        Be sure to utilize the Key Concepts for this segment of the lesson. Step 4: Complete the Dairy Breeds Check for Understanding . ·        The check for understanding is a short review of the content presented in the segment. Step 5: Complete the Dairy Decisions Activity. ·        Select dairy cattle breeds for the given scenarios. Step 6: Turn in the Dairy Decisions Activity .   Class 2 Essential Questions: 1.     What are the origins, physical characteristics, traits and usages of Asian and African breeds? 2.     What physical characteristics make these breeds well-suited to hot, humid climates?   Step 1: While viewing the image or video presented by your instructor, write down the first word which comes to mind. Be prepared to discuss your answer as a class. Step 2: View the Asian & African Breeds PowerPoint ® segment. ·        This segment is 10 slides long. ·        Be sure to utilize the Key Concepts for this segment of the lesson. ·        Slide 34: Discuss the physical adaptations of Asian and African breeds. Step 3: Complete the Asian & African Breeds Check for Understanding . ·        The check for understanding is a short review of the content presented in the segment. Step 4: Complete the Trivia Game Exit Ticket Activity , then turn it in before leaving class.   Class 3 Essential Questions: 1.     What are the origins, physical characteristics, traits and usages of British breeds?   Step 1: List some of the countries Asian and African breeds come from as a review. Step 2: View the British Breeds PowerPoint ® segment. ·        This segment is 14 slides long. ·        Be sure to utilize the Key Concepts for this segment of the lesson. ·        Slide 48: Discuss common traits among the British breeds. Step 3: Complete the British Breeds Check for Understanding . ·        The check for understanding is a short review of the content presented in the segment. Step 4: Begin the Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity . ·        Develop a set of flashcards to practice your knowledge of cattle breeds and their characteristics. Step 5: Provide a progress update on the Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity .   Class 4 Essential Questions: 1.     What are the origins, physical characteristics, traits and usages of continental breeds?   Step 1: Brainstorm answers to the question, “ which countries do continental cattle breeds originate from ”. Be prepared to discuss your responses.   Step 2: View the Continental Breeds PowerPoint ® segment. ·        This segment is 20 slides long. ·        Be sure to utilize the Key Concepts for this segment of the lesson. ·        Slide 68: Discuss the common traits of continental breeds. Step 3: Complete the Continental Breeds Check for Understanding . ·        The check for understanding is a short review of the content presented in the segment. Step 4: Continue the Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity . ·        Develop a set of flashcards to practice your knowledge of cattle breeds and their characteristics. Step 5: Write down three statements about the topic of the lesson, two truths and a lie . Once complete, exchange statements with a partner to figure out which statement is the lie.   Class 5 Essential Questions: 1.     What are the origins, physical characteristics, traits and usages of American breeds?   Step 1: Think, Pair, Share : Consider a response to the following question for one or two minutes before sharing your response in a small group.   ·        Cattle are not native to the U.S., meaning foundation stock was imported at some point. What are you expecting American breeds of cattle to be like? Step 2: View the American Breeds PowerPoint ® segment. ·        This segment is 17 slides long. ·        Be sure to utilize the Key Concepts for this segment of the lesson. Step 3: Complete the American Breeds Check for Understanding . ·        The check for understanding is a short review of the content presented in the segment. Step 4: Complete the Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity . ·        Develop a set of flashcards to practice your knowledge of cattle breeds and their characteristics. Step 5: Begin the Build a Breed Project . ·        Create your own crossbred or composite cattle breed which would suit your local area well. Step 6: Provide a progress update on the Build a Breed Project .   Class 6 Step 1: Define the terms purebred, crossbred and composite in your own words. Review the correct definitions as a class. Step 2: Continue the Build a Breed Project . ·        Create your own crossbred or composite cattle breed which would suit your local area well. Step 3: Provide a progress update on the Build a Breed Project .   Class 7 Step 1: Use the flashcards from the Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity to review for the assessment. Step 2: Complete the Breeds of Livestock: Cattle Final Assessment . ·        The assessment is a comprehensive assessment covering material throughout the entire lesson. Step 3: Complete the Build a Breed Project . ·        Create your own crossbred or composite cattle breed which would suit your local area well. Step 4: Turn in the Build a Breed Project .

Project Build a Breed   Project Overview: You will create your own crossbred or composite cattle breed which would suit your local area well.   Directions: 1.     Determine five ideal traits for a cattle breed which relate to your local area. ·       At least two of these traits should relate specifically to the climate and geography of your local area, considering: -       mildness or severity of the temperatures in each season -       mildness or severity of the precipitation (rainfall or snow) in each season -       how the temperature and weather affect pasture and crop production to provide feed for cattle -       major geographic features and their effect on cattle production, such as water resources, available grazing land and other factors -       how much space (stocking rate) would be needed for each animal based on these factors ·       Up to three of these may be production-based traits, such as milk production, growth rate, meat quality or aesthetics   2.     Review the breeds discussed in the lesson. Select breeds to base your new breed on. Your selection should be based on the ideal traits you identified. ·       Crossbred cattle are two breeds ·       Composite cattle are three or more breeds   3.     Based on the foundation breeds you chose, come up with the following information about your new breed: ·       Name of the new breed ·       Origin of the new breed -       specific farm, town, county or local region ·       Percentage or fraction of each foundation breed utilized ·       Five ideal traits it will possess and which foundation breed(s) addresses each of your five ideal traits ·       Physical characteristics of the new breed and specify which characteristics are from each foundation breed, including descriptions of items such as: -       frame size -       coat color, patterns, markings and light or dark points possible -       naturally horned (shape and size), polled or both -       hair type or length -       body type such as very skinny, fat, muscular or very muscular -       excess skin, presence of a hump or drooping ears   4.     When you have determined the information for your new breed, create a social media profile showcasing the new breed. This profile can be created on a poster paper or using graphic design software, but should include: ·       Cover photo showcasing one ideal trait of the new breed ·       Profile picture showing the physical characteristics of the new breed ·       About section featuring: -       new breed name and social media handle -       where the new breed is from -       what the foundation breeds are and their percentage or fraction ·       Two or three social media posts which highlight the remaining four ideal traits of the new breed   5.     Display your social media profile and take turns presenting your breed with classmates in a gallery walk.   6.     Once completed, turn in your summary of information on your new breed and the social media profile according to your instructor’s directions.   Rubric Description Possible Points Your Score Research & Organization: ·       Student researched the local area’s climate and geography to identify five ideal traits a new breed should posses ·       Social media profile is on paper or digital, but contains all necessary information and parts described: cover photo, profile picture, about section, two or three social media posts ·       Information was presented in a logical and organized manner 25   Concept & Understanding: ·       Understanding of advantageous traits of foundation breeds in the lesson is clearly evident ·       Logical thinking was utilized to address the ideal traits of the student’s local area ·       Student clearly explained why foundation breeds were chosen and what advantageous traits their new breed would inherit from each ·       New breed’s information is realistic, including: name, origin, percentage of foundation breeds, physical characteristics and ideal traits 35   Creativity/Craftmanship: ·       New breed and social media profile is unique and reflects the student’s or group’s individuality ·       Project is clearly a high-quality product 25   Production/Effort: ·       Class time provided for the project was used efficiently ·       Time and effort are evident in the execution of the project 15     Total Points 100

Lesson Plan Breeds of Livestock: Cattle   Lesson Overview Media: Microsoft ® PowerPoint ® Presentation (85 slides) Seat Time: 7 Classes | 350 minutes teaching   Goal: To provide students with the origins, physical characteristics, traits and usages of cattle breeds.   Description: This lesson helps students discover valuable information regarding the types of cattle raised in the world, as well as their origins, physical characteristics, traits and usages. Have students consider the question “what differences do you see physically in these three breeds of cattle, and how may this impact their use in livestock production”. Lead a discussion of their responses. Step 2: Distribute the Action Plan , Vocabulary Handout and Key Concepts . ·        The Action Plan lays out a list of tasks for students to complete during the lesson. ·        The Vocabulary Handout is a list of terms used throughout the lesson. ·        The Key Concepts is an outline which identifies the main ideas presented in the lesson which students can fill in to aid in note taking during the lesson. Step 3: Show the Dairy Breeds PowerPoint ® segment. ·        This segment is 24 slides long. ·        Be sure to utilize the Key Concepts for this segment of the lesson. Step 4: Administer the Dairy Breeds Check for Understanding . ·        The check for understanding is a short review of the content presented in the segment. Step 5: Students should complete the Dairy Decisions Activity. ·        Students will select dairy cattle breeds for the given scenarios. Step 6: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students turn in the Dairy Decisions Activity .   Class 2 Class Overview: Asian & African Breeds Microsoft ® PowerPoint ® Segment Action Plan Key Concepts Asian & African Breeds Check for Understanding Trivia Game Exit Ticket Activity   Essential Questions: 1.     What are the origins, physical characteristics, traits and usages of Asian and African breeds? 2.     What physical characteristics make these breeds well-suited to hot, humid climates?   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Show students an image or video of one of the breeds in this segment . Have students write down the first word which comes to mind. Discuss students’ answers as a class. Step 2: Show the Asian & African Breeds PowerPoint ® segment. ·        This segment is 10 slides long. ·        Be sure to utilize the Key Concepts for this segment of the lesson. ·        Slide 34: Have a discussion with students about the physical adaptations of Asian and African breeds. Step 3: Administer the Asian & African Breeds Check for Understanding . ·        The check for understanding is a short review of the content presented in the segment. Step 4: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students complete the Trivia Game Exit Ticket Activity , then turn it in before leaving class.   Class 3 Class Overview: British Breeds Microsoft ® PowerPoint ® Segment Action Plan Key Concepts British Breeds Check for Understanding Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity   Essential Questions: 1.     What are the origins, physical characteristics, traits and usages of British breeds?   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Have students list some of the countries Asian and African breeds come from as a review. Step 2: Show the British Breeds PowerPoint ® segment. ·        This segment is 14 slides long. ·        Be sure to utilize the Key Concepts for this segment of the lesson. ·        Slide 48: Have a discussion with students about common traits among the British breeds. Step 3: Administer the British Breeds Check for Understanding . ·        The check for understanding is a short review of the content presented in the segment. Step 4: Students should begin the Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity . ·        Students will develop a set of flashcards to practice their knowledge of cattle breeds and their characteristics. Step 5: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students provide a progress update on the Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity .   Class 4 Class Overview: Continental Breeds Microsoft ® PowerPoint ® Segment Action Plan Key Concepts Continental Breeds Check for Understanding Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity   Essential Questions: 1.     What are the origins, physical characteristics, traits and usages of continental breeds?   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Have students brainstorm answers to the question, “ which countries do continental cattle breeds originate from ”. Lead students to discuss their responses.   Step 2: Show the Continental Breeds PowerPoint ® segment. ·        This segment is 20 slides long. ·        Be sure to utilize the Key Concepts for this segment of the lesson. ·        Slide 68: Have a discussion with students about the common traits of continental breeds. Step 3: Administer the Continental Breeds Check for Understanding . ·        The check for understanding is a short review of the content presented in the segment. Step 4: Students should continue the Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity . ·        Students will develop a set of flashcards to practice their knowledge of cattle breeds and their characteristics. Step 5: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students write down three statements about the topic of the lesson, two truths and a lie . Once complete, students should exchange statements with a partner to figure out which statement is the lie.   Class 5 Class Overview: American Breeds Microsoft ® PowerPoint ® Segment Action Plan Key Concepts American Breeds Check for Understanding Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity Build a Breed Project   Essential Questions: 1.     What are the origins, physical characteristics, traits and usages of American breeds?   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Think, Pair, Share : Pose the following question to students and have them consider their response for one or two minutes before asking them to get into groups and share their responses.   -       Cattle are not native to the U.S., meaning foundation stock was imported at some point. What are you expecting American breeds of cattle to be like? Step 2: Show the American Breeds PowerPoint ® segment. ·        This segment is 17 slides long. ·        Be sure to utilize the Key Concepts for this segment of the lesson. Step 3: Administer the American Breeds Check for Understanding . ·        The check for understanding is a short review of the content presented in the segment. Step 4: Students should complete the Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity . ·        Students will develop a set of flashcards to practice their knowledge of cattle breeds and their characteristics. Step 5: Students should begin the Build a Breed Project . ·        Students will create their own crossbred or composite cattle breed which would suit their local area well. Step 6: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students provide a progress update on the Build a Breed Project .   Class 6 Class Overview: Action Plan Build a Breed Project   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Have students define the terms purebred, crossbred and composite in their own words. Review the correct definitions as a class. Step 2: Students should begin the Build a Breed Project . ·        Students will create their own crossbred or composite cattle breed which would suit their local area well. Step 3: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students provide a progress update on the Build a Breed Project .   Class 7 Class Overview: Action Plan Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity Breeds of Livestock: Cattle Final Assessment Build a Breed Project   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Have students use the flashcards from the Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity to review for the assessment. Step 2: Administer the Breeds of Livestock: Cattle Final Assessment . ·        The assessment is a comprehensive assessment covering material throughout the entire lesson. Step 3: Students should complete the Build a Breed Project . ·        Stude nts will create their own crossbred or composite cattle breed which would suit their local area well. Step 4: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students turn in their Build a Breed Project .   Activity Overview Dairy Decisions Students will select dairy cattle breeds for the given scenarios.   Accommodations : Have students work with a partner to complete the activity.   Modifications : Have students only respond to two scenarios.   Extension : Have students compare their answers with others and discuss the similarities or differences in their responses.     Trivia Game Exit Ticket In teams, students will compete against one another in a game of trivia about dairy, Asian and African cattle breeds.   Accommodations : Provide trivia questions both orally and in a written format for students to reference.   Modifications : Have students write their responses to only half of the trivia questions asked.   Extension : Have students come up with their own trivia questions to ask the other team.     Cattle Breed Flashcards Students will develop a set of flashcards to practice their knowledge of cattle breeds and their characteristics.   Accommodations : Provide students additional time as needed.   Modifications : Have students complete flashcards for only five to seven breeds.   Extension : Have students devise a review game utilizing their flashcards and play it.   Project Overview Build a Breed Students will create their own crossbred or composite cattle breed which would suit their local area well.   Accommodations: Allow students to work with a partner.   Modifications: Have students complete only half the required components of the project.   Extension: Have students debate on which new breed is best suited to the local area.   Career & Technical Student Organizations National FFA Organization Livestock Judging   Career Connections Using the Career Connections Activity allows students to explore careers associated with this lesson by viewing career interviews with various industry professionals. Students will learn the important roles and purposes cattle breeds have in livestock production.   Objectives: 1.     To identify breeds of cattle. 2.     To understand the origins and characteristics of cattle breeds. 3.     To analyze the importance of specific cattle breeds in livestock production.   Class 1 Class Overview: Dairy Breeds Microsoft ® PowerPoint ® Segment Action Plan Vocabulary Handout Key Concepts Dairy Breeds Check for Understanding Dairy Decisions Activity   Essential Questions: 1.     What general terminology is associated with cattle? 2.     What are the origins, physical characteristics, traits and usages of dairy breeds?   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Display an image of a Holstein cow, Brahman cow and Angus cow. Have students consider the question “what differences do you see physically in these three breeds of cattle, and how may this impact their use in livestock production”. Lead a discussion of their responses. Step 2: Distribute the Action Plan , Vocabulary Handout and Key Concepts . ·        The Action Plan lays out a list of tasks for students to complete during the lesson. ·        The Vocabulary Handout is a list of terms used throughout the lesson. ·        The Key Concepts is an outline which identifies the main ideas presented in the lesson which students can fill in to aid in note taking during the lesson. Step 3: Show the Dairy Breeds PowerPoint ® segment. ·        This segment is 24 slides long. ·        Be sure to utilize the Key Concepts for this segment of the lesson. Step 4: Administer the Dairy Breeds Check for Understanding . ·        The check for understanding is a short review of the content presented in the segment. Step 5: Students should complete the Dairy Decisions Activity. ·        Students will select dairy cattle breeds for the given scenarios. Step 6: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students turn in the Dairy Decisions Activity .   Class 2 Class Overview: Asian & African Breeds Microsoft ® PowerPoint ® Segment Action Plan Key Concepts Asian & African Breeds Check for Understanding Trivia Game Exit Ticket Activity   Essential Questions: 1.     What are the origins, physical characteristics, traits and usages of Asian and African breeds? 2.     What physical characteristics make these breeds well-suited to hot, humid climates?   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Show students an image or video of one of the breeds in this segment . Have students write down the first word which comes to mind. Discuss students’ answers as a class. Step 2: Show the Asian & African Breeds PowerPoint ® segment. ·        This segment is 10 slides long. ·        Be sure to utilize the Key Concepts for this segment of the lesson. ·        Slide 34: Have a discussion with students about the physical adaptations of Asian and African breeds. Step 3: Administer the Asian & African Breeds Check for Understanding . ·        The check for understanding is a short review of the content presented in the segment. Step 4: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students complete the Trivia Game Exit Ticket Activity , then turn it in before leaving class.   Class 3 Class Overview: British Breeds Microsoft ® PowerPoint ® Segment Action Plan Key Concepts British Breeds Check for Understanding Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity   Essential Questions: 1.     What are the origins, physical characteristics, traits and usages of British breeds?   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Have students list some of the countries Asian and African breeds come from as a review. Step 2: Show the British Breeds PowerPoint ® segment. ·        This segment is 14 slides long. ·        Be sure to utilize the Key Concepts for this segment of the lesson. ·        Slide 48: Have a discussion with students about common traits among the British breeds. Step 3: Administer the British Breeds Check for Understanding . ·        The check for understanding is a short review of the content presented in the segment. Step 4: Students should begin the Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity . ·        Students will develop a set of flashcards to practice their knowledge of cattle breeds and their characteristics. Step 5: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students provide a progress update on the Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity .   Class 4 Class Overview: Continental Breeds Microsoft ® PowerPoint ® Segment Action Plan Key Concepts Continental Breeds Check for Understanding Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity   Essential Questions: 1.     What are the origins, physical characteristics, traits and usages of continental breeds?   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Have students brainstorm answers to the question, “ which countries do continental cattle breeds originate from ”. Lead students to discuss their responses.   Step 2: Show the Continental Breeds PowerPoint ® segment. ·        This segment is 20 slides long. ·        Be sure to utilize the Key Concepts for this segment of the lesson. ·        Slide 68: Have a discussion with students about the common traits of continental breeds. Step 3: Administer the Continental Breeds Check for Understanding . ·        The check for understanding is a short review of the content presented in the segment. Step 4: Students should continue the Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity . ·        Students will develop a set of flashcards to practice their knowledge of cattle breeds and their characteristics. Step 5: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students write down three statements about the topic of the lesson, two truths and a lie . Once complete, students should exchange statements with a partner to figure out which statement is the lie.   Class 5 Class Overview: American Breeds Microsoft ® PowerPoint ® Segment Action Plan Key Concepts American Breeds Check for Understanding Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity Build a Breed Project   Essential Questions: 1.     What are the origins, physical characteristics, traits and usages of American breeds?   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Think, Pair, Share : Pose the following question to students and have them consider their response for one or two minutes before asking them to get into groups and share their responses.   -       Cattle are not native to the U.S., meaning foundation stock was imported at some point. What are you expecting American breeds of cattle to be like? Step 2: Show the American Breeds PowerPoint ® segment. ·        This segment is 17 slides long. ·        Be sure to utilize the Key Concepts for this segment of the lesson. Step 3: Administer the American Breeds Check for Understanding . ·        The check for understanding is a short review of the content presented in the segment. Step 4: Students should complete the Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity . ·        Students will develop a set of flashcards to practice their knowledge of cattle breeds and their characteristics. Step 5: Students should begin the Build a Breed Project . ·        Students will create their own crossbred or composite cattle breed which would suit their local area well. Step 6: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students provide a progress update on the Build a Breed Project .   Class 6 Class Overview: Action Plan Build a Breed Project   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Have students define the terms purebred, crossbred and composite in their own words. Review the correct definitions as a class. Step 2: Students should begin the Build a Breed Project . ·        Students will create their own crossbred or composite cattle breed which would suit their local area well. Step 3: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students provide a progress update on the Build a Breed Project .   Class 7 Class Overview: Action Plan Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity Breeds of Livestock: Cattle Final Assessment Build a Breed Project   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Have students use the flashcards from the Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity to review for the assessment. Step 2: Administer the Breeds of Livestock: Cattle Final Assessment . ·        The assessment is a comprehensive assessment covering material throughout the entire lesson. Step 3: Students should complete the Build a Breed Project . ·        Stude nts will create their own crossbred or composite cattle breed which would suit their local area well. Step 4: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students turn in their Build a Breed Project .   Activity Overview Dairy Decisions Students will select dairy cattle breeds for the given scenarios.   Accommodations : Have students work with a partner to complete the activity.   Modifications : Have students only respond to two scenarios.   Extension : Have students compare their answers with others and discuss the similarities or differences in their responses.     Trivia Game Exit Ticket In teams, students will compete against one another in a game of trivia about dairy, Asian and African cattle breeds.   Accommodations : Provide trivia questions both orally and in a written format for students to reference.   Modifications : Have students write their responses to only half of the trivia questions asked.   Extension : Have students come up with their own trivia questions to ask the other team.     Cattle Breed Flashcards Students will develop a set of flashcards to practice their knowledge of cattle breeds and their characteristics.   Accommodations : Provide students additional time as needed.   Modifications : Have students complete flashcards for only five to seven breeds.   Extension : Have students devise a review game utilizing their flashcards and play it.   Project Overview Build a Breed Students will create their own crossbred or composite cattle breed which would suit their local area well.   Accommodations: Allow students to work with a partner.   Modifications: Have students complete only half the required components of the project.   Extension: Have students debate on which new breed is best suited to the local area.   Career & Technical Student Organizations National FFA Organization Livestock Judging   Career Connections Using the Career Connections Activity allows students to explore careers associated with this lesson by viewing career interviews with various industry professionals. The career interviews are located in the Select Media drop-down menu on the lesson page. See the Career Connections Activity for more details. Dale Spencer, President-Elect, Nebraska Cattlemen Emmet Callahan, Cattle Buyer and Cattle Farmer Jim Johnson, Cattle Producer

Students will learn the important roles and purposes cattle breeds have in livestock production.   Objectives: 1.     To identify breeds of cattle. 2.     To understand the origins and characteristics of cattle breeds. 3.     To analyze the importance of specific cattle breeds in livestock production.   Class 1 Class Overview: Dairy Breeds Microsoft ® PowerPoint ® Segment Action Plan Vocabulary Handout Key Concepts Dairy Breeds Check for Understanding Dairy Decisions Activity   Essential Questions: 1.     What general terminology is associated with cattle? 2.     What are the origins, physical characteristics, traits and usages of dairy breeds?   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Display an image of a Holstein cow, Brahman cow and Angus cow. Have students consider the question “what differences do you see physically in these three breeds of cattle, and how may this impact their use in livestock production”. Lead a discussion of their responses. Step 2: Distribute the Action Plan , Vocabulary Handout and Key Concepts . ·        The Action Plan lays out a list of tasks for students to complete during the lesson. ·        The Vocabulary Handout is a list of terms used throughout the lesson. ·        The Key Concepts is an outline which identifies the main ideas presented in the lesson which students can fill in to aid in note taking during the lesson. Step 3: Show the Dairy Breeds PowerPoint ® segment. ·        This segment is 24 slides long. ·        Be sure to utilize the Key Concepts for this segment of the lesson. Step 4: Administer the Dairy Breeds Check for Understanding . ·        The check for understanding is a short review of the content presented in the segment. Step 5: Students should complete the Dairy Decisions Activity. ·        Students will select dairy cattle breeds for the given scenarios. Step 6: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students turn in the Dairy Decisions Activity .   Class 2 Class Overview: Asian & African Breeds Microsoft ® PowerPoint ® Segment Action Plan Key Concepts Asian & African Breeds Check for Understanding Trivia Game Exit Ticket Activity   Essential Questions: 1.     What are the origins, physical characteristics, traits and usages of Asian and African breeds? 2.     What physical characteristics make these breeds well-suited to hot, humid climates?   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Show students an image or video of one of the breeds in this segment . Have students write down the first word which comes to mind. Discuss students’ answers as a class. Step 2: Show the Asian & African Breeds PowerPoint ® segment. ·        This segment is 10 slides long. ·        Be sure to utilize the Key Concepts for this segment of the lesson. ·        Slide 34: Have a discussion with students about the physical adaptations of Asian and African breeds. Step 3: Administer the Asian & African Breeds Check for Understanding . ·        The check for understanding is a short review of the content presented in the segment. Step 4: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students complete the Trivia Game Exit Ticket Activity , then turn it in before leaving class.   Class 3 Class Overview: British Breeds Microsoft ® PowerPoint ® Segment Action Plan Key Concepts British Breeds Check for Understanding Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity   Essential Questions: 1.     What are the origins, physical characteristics, traits and usages of British breeds?   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Have students list some of the countries Asian and African breeds come from as a review. Step 2: Show the British Breeds PowerPoint ® segment. ·        This segment is 14 slides long. ·        Be sure to utilize the Key Concepts for this segment of the lesson. ·        Slide 48: Have a discussion with students about common traits among the British breeds. Step 3: Administer the British Breeds Check for Understanding . ·        The check for understanding is a short review of the content presented in the segment. Step 4: Students should begin the Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity . ·        Students will develop a set of flashcards to practice their knowledge of cattle breeds and their characteristics. Step 5: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students provide a progress update on the Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity .   Class 4 Class Overview: Continental Breeds Microsoft ® PowerPoint ® Segment Action Plan Key Concepts Continental Breeds Check for Understanding Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity   Essential Questions: 1.     What are the origins, physical characteristics, traits and usages of continental breeds?   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Have students brainstorm answers to the question, “ which countries do continental cattle breeds originate from ”. Lead students to discuss their responses.   Step 2: Show the Continental Breeds PowerPoint ® segment. ·        This segment is 20 slides long. ·        Be sure to utilize the Key Concepts for this segment of the lesson. ·        Slide 68: Have a discussion with students about the common traits of continental breeds. Step 3: Administer the Continental Breeds Check for Understanding . ·        The check for understanding is a short review of the content presented in the segment. Step 4: Students should continue the Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity . ·        Students will develop a set of flashcards to practice their knowledge of cattle breeds and their characteristics. Step 5: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students write down three statements about the topic of the lesson, two truths and a lie . Once complete, students should exchange statements with a partner to figure out which statement is the lie.   Class 5 Class Overview: American Breeds Microsoft ® PowerPoint ® Segment Action Plan Key Concepts American Breeds Check for Understanding Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity Build a Breed Project   Essential Questions: 1.     What are the origins, physical characteristics, traits and usages of American breeds?   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Think, Pair, Share : Pose the following question to students and have them consider their response for one or two minutes before asking them to get into groups and share their responses.   -       Cattle are not native to the U.S., meaning foundation stock was imported at some point. What are you expecting American breeds of cattle to be like? Step 2: Show the American Breeds PowerPoint ® segment. ·        This segment is 17 slides long. ·        Be sure to utilize the Key Concepts for this segment of the lesson. Step 3: Administer the American Breeds Check for Understanding . ·        The check for understanding is a short review of the content presented in the segment. Step 4: Students should complete the Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity . ·        Students will develop a set of flashcards to practice their knowledge of cattle breeds and their characteristics. Step 5: Students should begin the Build a Breed Project . ·        Students will create their own crossbred or composite cattle breed which would suit their local area well. Step 6: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students provide a progress update on the Build a Breed Project .   Class 6 Class Overview: Action Plan Build a Breed Project   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Have students define the terms purebred, crossbred and composite in their own words. Review the correct definitions as a class. Step 2: Students should begin the Build a Breed Project . ·        Students will create their own crossbred or composite cattle breed which would suit their local area well. Step 3: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students provide a progress update on the Build a Breed Project .   Class 7 Class Overview: Action Plan Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity Breeds of Livestock: Cattle Final Assessment Build a Breed Project   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Have students use the flashcards from the Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity to review for the assessment. Step 2: Administer the Breeds of Livestock: Cattle Final Assessment . ·        The assessment is a comprehensive assessment covering material throughout the entire lesson. Step 3: Students should complete the Build a Breed Project . ·        Stude nts will create their own crossbred or composite cattle breed which would suit their local area well. Step 4: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students turn in their Build a Breed Project .   Activity Overview Dairy Decisions Students will select dairy cattle breeds for the given scenarios.   Accommodations : Have students work with a partner to complete the activity.   Modifications : Have students only respond to two scenarios.   Extension : Have students compare their answers with others and discuss the similarities or differences in their responses.     Trivia Game Exit Ticket In teams, students will compete against one another in a game of trivia about dairy, Asian and African cattle breeds.   Accommodations : Provide trivia questions both orally and in a written format for students to reference.   Modifications : Have students write their responses to only half of the trivia questions asked.   Extension : Have students come up with their own trivia questions to ask the other team.     Cattle Breed Flashcards Students will develop a set of flashcards to practice their knowledge of cattle breeds and their characteristics.   Accommodations : Provide students additional time as needed.   Modifications : Have students complete flashcards for only five to seven breeds.   Extension : Have students devise a review game utilizing their flashcards and play it.   Project Overview Build a Breed Students will create their own crossbred or composite cattle breed which would suit their local area well.   Accommodations: Allow students to work with a partner.   Modifications: Have students complete only half the required components of the project.   Extension: Have students debate on which new breed is best suited to the local area.   Career & Technical Student Organizations National FFA Organization Livestock Judging   Career Connections Using the Career Connections Activity allows students to explore careers associated with this lesson by viewing career interviews with various industry professionals. The career interviews are located in the Select Media drop-down menu on the lesson page. See the Career Connections Activity for more details. Dale Spencer, President-Elect, Nebraska Cattlemen Emmet Callahan, Cattle Buyer and Cattle Farmer Jim Johnson, Cattle Producer

Students will learn the important roles and purposes cattle breeds have in livestock production.   Objectives: 1.     To identify breeds of cattle. 2.     To understand the origins and characteristics of cattle breeds. 3.     To analyze the importance of specific cattle breeds in livestock production.   Class 1 Class Overview: Dairy Breeds Microsoft ® PowerPoint ® Segment Action Plan Vocabulary Handout Key Concepts Dairy Breeds Check for Understanding Dairy Decisions Activity   Essential Questions: 1.     What general terminology is associated with cattle? 2.     What are the origins, physical characteristics, traits and usages of dairy breeds?   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Display an image of a Holstein cow, Brahman cow and Angus cow. Have students consider the question “what differences do you see physically in these three breeds of cattle, and how may this impact their use in livestock production”. Lead a discussion of their responses. Step 2: Distribute the Action Plan , Vocabulary Handout and Key Concepts . ·        The Action Plan lays out a list of tasks for students to complete during the lesson. ·        The Vocabulary Handout is a list of terms used throughout the lesson. ·        The Key Concepts is an outline which identifies the main ideas presented in the lesson which students can fill in to aid in note taking during the lesson. Step 3: Show the Dairy Breeds PowerPoint ® segment. ·        This segment is 24 slides long. ·        Be sure to utilize the Key Concepts for this segment of the lesson. Step 4: Administer the Dairy Breeds Check for Understanding . ·        The check for understanding is a short review of the content presented in the segment. Step 5: Students should complete the Dairy Decisions Activity. ·        Students will select dairy cattle breeds for the given scenarios. Step 6: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students turn in the Dairy Decisions Activity .   Class 2 Class Overview: Asian & African Breeds Microsoft ® PowerPoint ® Segment Action Plan Key Concepts Asian & African Breeds Check for Understanding Trivia Game Exit Ticket Activity   Essential Questions: 1.     What are the origins, physical characteristics, traits and usages of Asian and African breeds? 2.     What physical characteristics make these breeds well-suited to hot, humid climates?   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Show students an image or video of one of the breeds in this segment . Have students write down the first word which comes to mind. Discuss students’ answers as a class. Step 2: Show the Asian & African Breeds PowerPoint ® segment. ·        This segment is 10 slides long. ·        Be sure to utilize the Key Concepts for this segment of the lesson. ·        Slide 34: Have a discussion with students about the physical adaptations of Asian and African breeds. Step 3: Administer the Asian & African Breeds Check for Understanding . ·        The check for understanding is a short review of the content presented in the segment. Step 4: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students complete the Trivia Game Exit Ticket Activity , then turn it in before leaving class.   Class 3 Class Overview: British Breeds Microsoft ® PowerPoint ® Segment Action Plan Key Concepts British Breeds Check for Understanding Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity   Essential Questions: 1.     What are the origins, physical characteristics, traits and usages of British breeds?   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Have students list some of the countries Asian and African breeds come from as a review. Step 2: Show the British Breeds PowerPoint ® segment. ·        This segment is 14 slides long. ·        Be sure to utilize the Key Concepts for this segment of the lesson. ·        Slide 48: Have a discussion with students about common traits among the British breeds. Step 3: Administer the British Breeds Check for Understanding . ·        The check for understanding is a short review of the content presented in the segment. Step 4: Students should begin the Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity . ·        Students will develop a set of flashcards to practice their knowledge of cattle breeds and their characteristics. Step 5: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students provide a progress update on the Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity .   Class 4 Class Overview: Continental Breeds Microsoft ® PowerPoint ® Segment Action Plan Key Concepts Continental Breeds Check for Understanding Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity   Essential Questions: 1.     What are the origins, physical characteristics, traits and usages of continental breeds?   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Have students brainstorm answers to the question, “ which countries do continental cattle breeds originate from ”. Lead students to discuss their responses.   Step 2: Show the Continental Breeds PowerPoint ® segment. ·        This segment is 20 slides long. ·        Be sure to utilize the Key Concepts for this segment of the lesson. ·        Slide 68: Have a discussion with students about the common traits of continental breeds. Step 3: Administer the Continental Breeds Check for Understanding . ·        The check for understanding is a short review of the content presented in the segment. Step 4: Students should continue the Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity . ·        Students will develop a set of flashcards to practice their knowledge of cattle breeds and their characteristics. Step 5: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students write down three statements about the topic of the lesson, two truths and a lie . Once complete, students should exchange statements with a partner to figure out which statement is the lie.   Class 5 Class Overview: American Breeds Microsoft ® PowerPoint ® Segment Action Plan Key Concepts American Breeds Check for Understanding Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity Build a Breed Project   Essential Questions: 1.     What are the origins, physical characteristics, traits and usages of American breeds?   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Think, Pair, Share : Pose the following question to students and have them consider their response for one or two minutes before asking them to get into groups and share their responses.   -       Cattle are not native to the U.S., meaning foundation stock was imported at some point. What are you expecting American breeds of cattle to be like? Step 2: Show the American Breeds PowerPoint ® segment. ·        This segment is 17 slides long. ·        Be sure to utilize the Key Concepts for this segment of the lesson. Step 3: Administer the American Breeds Check for Understanding . ·        The check for understanding is a short review of the content presented in the segment. Step 4: Students should complete the Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity . ·        Students will develop a set of flashcards to practice their knowledge of cattle breeds and their characteristics. Step 5: Students should begin the Build a Breed Project . ·        Students will create their own crossbred or composite cattle breed which would suit their local area well. Step 6: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students provide a progress update on the Build a Breed Project .   Class 6 Class Overview: Action Plan Build a Breed Project   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Have students define the terms purebred, crossbred and composite in their own words. Review the correct definitions as a class. Step 2: Students should begin the Build a Breed Project . ·        Students will create their own crossbred or composite cattle breed which would suit their local area well. Step 3: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students provide a progress update on the Build a Breed Project .   Class 7 Class Overview: Action Plan Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity Breeds of Livestock: Cattle Final Assessment Build a Breed Project   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Have students use the flashcards from the Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity to review for the assessment. Step 2: Administer the Breeds of Livestock: Cattle Final Assessment . ·        The assessment is a comprehensive assessment covering material throughout the entire lesson. Step 3: Students should complete the Build a Breed Project . ·        Stude nts will create their own crossbred or composite cattle breed which would suit their local area well. Step 4: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students turn in their Build a Breed Project .   Activity Overview Dairy Decisions Students will select dairy cattle breeds for the given scenarios.   Accommodations : Have students work with a partner to complete the activity.   Modifications : Have students only respond to two scenarios.   Extension : Have students compare their answers with others and discuss the similarities or differences in their responses.     Trivia Game Exit Ticket In teams, students will compete against one another in a game of trivia about dairy, Asian and African cattle breeds.   Accommodations : Provide trivia questions both orally and in a written format for students to reference.   Modifications : Have students write their responses to only half of the trivia questions asked.   Extension : Have students come up with their own trivia questions to ask the other team.     Cattle Breed Flashcards Students will develop a set of flashcards to practice their knowledge of cattle breeds and their characteristics.   Accommodations : Provide students additional time as needed.   Modifications : Have students complete flashcards for only five to seven breeds.   Extension : Have students devise a review game utilizing their flashcards and play it.   Project Overview Build a Breed Students will create their own crossbred or composite cattle breed which would suit their local area well.   Accommodations: Allow students to work with a partner.   Modifications: Have students complete only half the required components of the project.   Extension: Have students debate on which new breed is best suited to the local area.   Career & Technical Student Organizations National FFA Organization Livestock Judging   Career Connections Using the Career Connections Activity allows students to explore careers associated with this lesson by viewing career interviews with various industry professionals. The career interviews are located in the Select Media drop-down menu on the lesson page. See the Career Connections Activity for more details. Dale Spencer, President-Elect, Nebraska Cattlemen Emmet Callahan, Cattle Buyer and Cattle Farmer Jim Johnson, Cattle Producer

Students will learn the important roles and purposes cattle breeds have in livestock production.   Objectives: 1.     To identify breeds of cattle. 2.     To understand the origins and characteristics of cattle breeds. 3.     To analyze the importance of specific cattle breeds in livestock production.   Class 1 Class Overview: Dairy Breeds Microsoft ® PowerPoint ® Segment Action Plan Vocabulary Handout Key Concepts Dairy Breeds Check for Understanding Dairy Decisions Activity   Essential Questions: 1.     What general terminology is associated with cattle? 2.     What are the origins, physical characteristics, traits and usages of dairy breeds?   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Display an image of a Holstein cow, Brahman cow and Angus cow. Have students consider the question “what differences do you see physically in these three breeds of cattle, and how may this impact their use in livestock production”. Lead a discussion of their responses. Step 2: Distribute the Action Plan , Vocabulary Handout and Key Concepts . ·        The Action Plan lays out a list of tasks for students to complete during the lesson. ·        The Vocabulary Handout is a list of terms used throughout the lesson. ·        The Key Concepts is an outline which identifies the main ideas presented in the lesson which students can fill in to aid in note taking during the lesson. Step 3: Show the Dairy Breeds PowerPoint ® segment. ·        This segment is 24 slides long. ·        Be sure to utilize the Key Concepts for this segment of the lesson. Step 4: Administer the Dairy Breeds Check for Understanding . ·        The check for understanding is a short review of the content presented in the segment. Step 5: Students should complete the Dairy Decisions Activity. ·        Students will select dairy cattle breeds for the given scenarios. Step 6: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students turn in the Dairy Decisions Activity .   Class 2 Class Overview: Asian & African Breeds Microsoft ® PowerPoint ® Segment Action Plan Key Concepts Asian & African Breeds Check for Understanding Trivia Game Exit Ticket Activity   Essential Questions: 1.     What are the origins, physical characteristics, traits and usages of Asian and African breeds? 2.     What physical characteristics make these breeds well-suited to hot, humid climates?   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Show students an image or video of one of the breeds in this segment . Have students write down the first word which comes to mind. Discuss students’ answers as a class. Step 2: Show the Asian & African Breeds PowerPoint ® segment. ·        This segment is 10 slides long. ·        Be sure to utilize the Key Concepts for this segment of the lesson. ·        Slide 34: Have a discussion with students about the physical adaptations of Asian and African breeds. Step 3: Administer the Asian & African Breeds Check for Understanding . ·        The check for understanding is a short review of the content presented in the segment. Step 4: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students complete the Trivia Game Exit Ticket Activity , then turn it in before leaving class.   Class 3 Class Overview: British Breeds Microsoft ® PowerPoint ® Segment Action Plan Key Concepts British Breeds Check for Understanding Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity   Essential Questions: 1.     What are the origins, physical characteristics, traits and usages of British breeds?   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Have students list some of the countries Asian and African breeds come from as a review. Step 2: Show the British Breeds PowerPoint ® segment. ·        This segment is 14 slides long. ·        Be sure to utilize the Key Concepts for this segment of the lesson. ·        Slide 48: Have a discussion with students about common traits among the British breeds. Step 3: Administer the British Breeds Check for Understanding . ·        The check for understanding is a short review of the content presented in the segment. Step 4: Students should begin the Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity . ·        Students will develop a set of flashcards to practice their knowledge of cattle breeds and their characteristics. Step 5: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students provide a progress update on the Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity .   Class 4 Class Overview: Continental Breeds Microsoft ® PowerPoint ® Segment Action Plan Key Concepts Continental Breeds Check for Understanding Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity   Essential Questions: 1.     What are the origins, physical characteristics, traits and usages of continental breeds?   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Have students brainstorm answers to the question, “ which countries do continental cattle breeds originate from ”. Lead students to discuss their responses.   Step 2: Show the Continental Breeds PowerPoint ® segment. ·        This segment is 20 slides long. ·        Be sure to utilize the Key Concepts for this segment of the lesson. ·        Slide 68: Have a discussion with students about the common traits of continental breeds. Step 3: Administer the Continental Breeds Check for Understanding . ·        The check for understanding is a short review of the content presented in the segment. Step 4: Students should continue the Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity . ·        Students will develop a set of flashcards to practice their knowledge of cattle breeds and their characteristics. Step 5: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students write down three statements about the topic of the lesson, two truths and a lie . Once complete, students should exchange statements with a partner to figure out which statement is the lie.   Class 5 Class Overview: American Breeds Microsoft ® PowerPoint ® Segment Action Plan Key Concepts American Breeds Check for Understanding Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity Build a Breed Project   Essential Questions: 1.     What are the origins, physical characteristics, traits and usages of American breeds?   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Think, Pair, Share : Pose the following question to students and have them consider their response for one or two minutes before asking them to get into groups and share their responses.   -       Cattle are not native to the U.S., meaning foundation stock was imported at some point. What are you expecting American breeds of cattle to be like? Step 2: Show the American Breeds PowerPoint ® segment. ·        This segment is 17 slides long. ·        Be sure to utilize the Key Concepts for this segment of the lesson. Step 3: Administer the American Breeds Check for Understanding . ·        The check for understanding is a short review of the content presented in the segment. Step 4: Students should complete the Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity . ·        Students will develop a set of flashcards to practice their knowledge of cattle breeds and their characteristics. Step 5: Students should begin the Build a Breed Project . ·        Students will create their own crossbred or composite cattle breed which would suit their local area well. Step 6: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students provide a progress update on the Build a Breed Project .   Class 6 Class Overview: Action Plan Build a Breed Project   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Have students define the terms purebred, crossbred and composite in their own words. Review the correct definitions as a class. Step 2: Students should begin the Build a Breed Project . ·        Students will create their own crossbred or composite cattle breed which would suit their local area well. Step 3: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students provide a progress update on the Build a Breed Project .   Class 7 Class Overview: Action Plan Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity Breeds of Livestock: Cattle Final Assessment Build a Breed Project   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Have students use the flashcards from the Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity to review for the assessment. Step 2: Administer the Breeds of Livestock: Cattle Final Assessment . ·        The assessment is a comprehensive assessment covering material throughout the entire lesson. Step 3: Students should complete the Build a Breed Project . ·        Stude nts will create their own crossbred or composite cattle breed which would suit their local area well. Step 4: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students turn in their Build a Breed Project .   Activity Overview Dairy Decisions Students will select dairy cattle breeds for the given scenarios.   Accommodations : Have students work with a partner to complete the activity.   Modifications : Have students only respond to two scenarios.   Extension : Have students compare their answers with others and discuss the similarities or differences in their responses.     Trivia Game Exit Ticket In teams, students will compete against one another in a game of trivia about dairy, Asian and African cattle breeds.   Accommodations : Provide trivia questions both orally and in a written format for students to reference.   Modifications : Have students write their responses to only half of the trivia questions asked.   Extension : Have students come up with their own trivia questions to ask the other team.     Cattle Breed Flashcards Students will develop a set of flashcards to practice their knowledge of cattle breeds and their characteristics.   Accommodations : Provide students additional time as needed.   Modifications : Have students complete flashcards for only five to seven breeds.   Extension : Have students devise a review game utilizing their flashcards and play it.   Project Overview Build a Breed Students will create their own crossbred or composite cattle breed which would suit their local area well.   Accommodations: Allow students to work with a partner.   Modifications: Have students complete only half the required components of the project.   Extension: Have students debate on which new breed is best suited to the local area.   Career & Technical Student Organizations National FFA Organization Livestock Judging   Career Connections Using the Career Connections Activity allows students to explore careers associated with this lesson by viewing career interviews with various industry professionals. The career interviews are located in the Select Media drop-down menu on the lesson page. See the Career Connections Activity for more details. Dale Spencer, President-Elect, Nebraska Cattlemen Emmet Callahan, Cattle Buyer and Cattle Farmer Jim Johnson, Cattle Producer

Students will learn the important roles and purposes cattle breeds have in livestock production.   Objectives: 1.     To identify breeds of cattle. 2.     To understand the origins and characteristics of cattle breeds. 3.     To analyze the importance of specific cattle breeds in livestock production.   Class 1 Class Overview: Dairy Breeds Microsoft ® PowerPoint ® Segment Action Plan Vocabulary Handout Key Concepts Dairy Breeds Check for Understanding Dairy Decisions Activity   Essential Questions: 1.     What general terminology is associated with cattle? 2.     What are the origins, physical characteristics, traits and usages of dairy breeds?   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Display an image of a Holstein cow, Brahman cow and Angus cow. Have students consider the question “what differences do you see physically in these three breeds of cattle, and how may this impact their use in livestock production”. Lead a discussion of their responses. Step 2: Distribute the Action Plan , Vocabulary Handout and Key Concepts . ·        The Action Plan lays out a list of tasks for students to complete during the lesson. ·        The Vocabulary Handout is a list of terms used throughout the lesson. ·        The Key Concepts is an outline which identifies the main ideas presented in the lesson which students can fill in to aid in note taking during the lesson. Step 3: Show the Dairy Breeds PowerPoint ® segment. ·        This segment is 24 slides long. ·        Be sure to utilize the Key Concepts for this segment of the lesson. Step 4: Administer the Dairy Breeds Check for Understanding . ·        The check for understanding is a short review of the content presented in the segment. Step 5: Students should complete the Dairy Decisions Activity. ·        Students will select dairy cattle breeds for the given scenarios. Step 6: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students turn in the Dairy Decisions Activity .   Class 2 Class Overview: Asian & African Breeds Microsoft ® PowerPoint ® Segment Action Plan Key Concepts Asian & African Breeds Check for Understanding Trivia Game Exit Ticket Activity   Essential Questions: 1.     What are the origins, physical characteristics, traits and usages of Asian and African breeds? 2.     What physical characteristics make these breeds well-suited to hot, humid climates?   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Show students an image or video of one of the breeds in this segment . Have students write down the first word which comes to mind. Discuss students’ answers as a class. Step 2: Show the Asian & African Breeds PowerPoint ® segment. ·        This segment is 10 slides long. ·        Be sure to utilize the Key Concepts for this segment of the lesson. ·        Slide 34: Have a discussion with students about the physical adaptations of Asian and African breeds. Step 3: Administer the Asian & African Breeds Check for Understanding . ·        The check for understanding is a short review of the content presented in the segment. Step 4: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students complete the Trivia Game Exit Ticket Activity , then turn it in before leaving class.   Class 3 Class Overview: British Breeds Microsoft ® PowerPoint ® Segment Action Plan Key Concepts British Breeds Check for Understanding Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity   Essential Questions: 1.     What are the origins, physical characteristics, traits and usages of British breeds?   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Have students list some of the countries Asian and African breeds come from as a review. Step 2: Show the British Breeds PowerPoint ® segment. ·        This segment is 14 slides long. ·        Be sure to utilize the Key Concepts for this segment of the lesson. ·        Slide 48: Have a discussion with students about common traits among the British breeds. Step 3: Administer the British Breeds Check for Understanding . ·        The check for understanding is a short review of the content presented in the segment. Step 4: Students should begin the Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity . ·        Students will develop a set of flashcards to practice their knowledge of cattle breeds and their characteristics. Step 5: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students provide a progress update on the Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity .   Class 4 Class Overview: Continental Breeds Microsoft ® PowerPoint ® Segment Action Plan Key Concepts Continental Breeds Check for Understanding Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity   Essential Questions: 1.     What are the origins, physical characteristics, traits and usages of continental breeds?   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Have students brainstorm answers to the question, “ which countries do continental cattle breeds originate from ”. Lead students to discuss their responses.   Step 2: Show the Continental Breeds PowerPoint ® segment. ·        This segment is 20 slides long. ·        Be sure to utilize the Key Concepts for this segment of the lesson. ·        Slide 68: Have a discussion with students about the common traits of continental breeds. Step 3: Administer the Continental Breeds Check for Understanding . ·        The check for understanding is a short review of the content presented in the segment. Step 4: Students should continue the Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity . ·        Students will develop a set of flashcards to practice their knowledge of cattle breeds and their characteristics. Step 5: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students write down three statements about the topic of the lesson, two truths and a lie . Once complete, students should exchange statements with a partner to figure out which statement is the lie.   Class 5 Class Overview: American Breeds Microsoft ® PowerPoint ® Segment Action Plan Key Concepts American Breeds Check for Understanding Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity Build a Breed Project   Essential Questions: 1.     What are the origins, physical characteristics, traits and usages of American breeds?   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Think, Pair, Share : Pose the following question to students and have them consider their response for one or two minutes before asking them to get into groups and share their responses.   -       Cattle are not native to the U.S., meaning foundation stock was imported at some point. What are you expecting American breeds of cattle to be like? Step 2: Show the American Breeds PowerPoint ® segment. ·        This segment is 17 slides long. ·        Be sure to utilize the Key Concepts for this segment of the lesson. Step 3: Administer the American Breeds Check for Understanding . ·        The check for understanding is a short review of the content presented in the segment. Step 4: Students should complete the Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity . ·        Students will develop a set of flashcards to practice their knowledge of cattle breeds and their characteristics. Step 5: Students should begin the Build a Breed Project . ·        Students will create their own crossbred or composite cattle breed which would suit their local area well. Step 6: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students provide a progress update on the Build a Breed Project .   Class 6 Class Overview: Action Plan Build a Breed Project   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Have students define the terms purebred, crossbred and composite in their own words. Review the correct definitions as a class. Step 2: Students should begin the Build a Breed Project . ·        Students will create their own crossbred or composite cattle breed which would suit their local area well. Step 3: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students provide a progress update on the Build a Breed Project .   Class 7 Class Overview: Action Plan Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity Breeds of Livestock: Cattle Final Assessment Build a Breed Project   Step 1: Bell Ringer: ·        Have students use the flashcards from the Cattle Breeds Flashcards Activity to review for the assessment. Step 2: Administer the Breeds of Livestock: Cattle Final Assessment . ·        The assessment is a comprehensive assessment covering material throughout the entire lesson. Step 3: Students should complete the Build a Breed Project . ·        Stude nts will create their own crossbred or composite cattle breed which would suit their local area well. Step 4: Exit Ticket: ·        Have students turn in their Build a Breed Project .   Activity Overview Dairy Decisions Students will select dairy cattle breeds for the given scenarios.   Accommodations : Have students work with a partner to complete the activity.   Modifications : Have students only respond to two scenarios.   Extension : Have students compare their answers with others and discuss the similarities or differences in their responses.     Trivia Game Exit Ticket In teams, students will compete against one another in a game of trivia about dairy, Asian and African cattle breeds.   Accommodations : Provide trivia questions both orally and in a written format for students to reference.   Modifications : Have students write their responses to only half of the trivia questions asked.   Extension : Have students come up with their own trivia questions to ask the other team.     Cattle Breed Flashcards Students will develop a set of flashcards to practice their knowledge of cattle breeds and their characteristics.   Accommodations : Provide students additional time as needed.   Modifications : Have students complete flashcards for only five to seven breeds.   Extension : Have students devise a review game utilizing their flashcards and play it.   Project Overview Build a Breed Students will create their own crossbred or composite cattle breed which would suit their local area well.   Accommodations: Allow students to work with a partner.   Modifications: Have students complete only half the required components of the project.   Extension: Have students debate on which new breed is best suited to the local area.   Career & Technical Student Organizations National FFA Organization Livestock Judging   Career Connections Using the Career Connections Activity allows students to explore careers associated with this lesson by viewing career interviews with various industry professionals. The career interviews are located in the Select Media drop-down menu on the lesson page. See the Career Connections Activity for more details. Dale Spencer, President-Elect, Nebraska Cattlemen Emmet Callahan, Cattle Buyer and Cattle Farmer Jim Johnson, Cattle Producer
